## Headline results (threshold 0.90, n = 36)

Run 3 / run 4 are the two complete one-call runs.

| Path | TP/FP/FN/TN (run 3) | Precision | Recall | F1 | P (mean±SD) | R (mean±SD) | F1 (mean±SD) | Per-case stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RULES | 1/0/18/17 | 1.000 [0.000, 1.000] | 0.053 [0.000, 0.174] | 0.100 [0.000, 0.296] | 1.000 ± 0.000 | 0.053 ± 0.000 | 0.100 ± 0.000 | 1.000 |
| LLM-only | 18/7/1/10 | 0.720 [0.536, 0.889] | 0.947 [0.818, 1.000] | 0.818 [0.667, 0.927] | 0.740 ± 0.028 | 0.974 ± 0.037 | 0.841 ± 0.032 | 0.778 |
| HYBRID | 18/7/1/10 | 0.720 [0.536, 0.889] | 0.947 [0.818, 1.000] | 0.818 [0.667, 0.927] | 0.740 ± 0.028 | 0.974 ± 0.037 | 0.841 ± 0.032 | 0.778 |

95% CIs are percentile bootstrap (5 000 resamples, seed 42). "Per-case
stability" = fraction of the 36 cases with an identical verdict **and**
defect type in both complete runs.

### At the BR-10 production threshold (0.70)

| Path | TP/FP/FN/TN (run 3) | Precision | Recall | F1 | Per-case stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RULES | 13/1/6/16 | 0.929 [0.765, 1.000] | 0.684 [0.467, 0.889] | 0.788 [0.606, 0.923] | 1.000 |
| LLM-only | 19/11/0/6 | 0.633 [0.462, 0.794] | 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] | 0.776 [0.632, 0.885] | 0.861 |
| HYBRID | 19/11/0/6 | 0.633 [0.461, 0.800] | 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] | 0.776 [0.632, 0.889] | 0.861 |

Lowering the threshold to 0.70 raises recall to 1.000 for both LLM paths and
costs 11 false positives, i.e. F1 falls from 0.818 to 0.776. This is why the
0.90 threshold is the reported one; both thresholds are in the paper.

### Per-category (threshold 0.90, run 3)

| Category | n | LLM-only TP/FP/FN | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ambiguity | 15 | 15 / 4 / 0 | 0.789 | 1.000 [0.796, 1.000] | 0.882 |
| Incomplete | 1 | 0 / 6 / 1 | 0.000 | 0.000 [0.000, 0.793] | 0.000 |
| Inconsistency | 2 | 0 / 0 / 2 | 0.000 | 0.000 [0.000, 0.658] | 0.000 |
| Unverifiable | 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0.000 | 0.000 [0.000, 0.793] | 0.000 |

Macro-F1 over the 4 categories = 0.221. **The LLM detects ambiguity almost
perfectly, but its category labels are weak.** Of the 4 non-ambiguity
defective cases, 3 were flagged as a defect but **mislabelled** (2 as
"ambiguity" rather than their true category) and only 1 (TC-101,
"incomplete") was both detected and given the correct category; in run 3 one
case (TC-055, "inconsistency") was missed entirely. The 7 false positives are
mostly "incomplete" (6) plus 1 "ambiguity". So the high binary recall
(0.947) is *not* evidence that the tool identifies defect *types* correctly.
Because three categories have n ≤ 2, their per-category numbers carry
essentially no statistical weight and must be reported with that caveat (this
is a benchmark-composition limitation, not a clean result).

## Paired comparisons (McNemar exact, run 3, threshold 0.90)

| Comparison | Only A correct | Only B correct | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| RULES vs LLM-only | 8 | 18 | 0.076 |
| RULES vs HYBRID | 8 | 18 | 0.076 |
| LLM-only vs HYBRID | 0 | 0 | 1.000 |

Run 4 gives the same picture with p = 0.023 (6 vs 18 discordant pairs).
Report the run-3 value and the run-4 value together, or report the range
0.023–0.076; do not pick the smaller one.

**LLM-only and HYBRID are identical** in the one-call harness: the hybrid
path falls back to rules only when the LLM returns no usable defects, and
the LLM answered every case, so the two paths coincide. The
rules-vs-LLM difference is not significant at α = 0.05 in run 3 (p = 0.076).

## Limitations to state in the paper

1. **One provider profile.** The second profile (OVHcloud) was attempted and
   returned HTTP 403 on every request; it produced no usable result and is
   **not** reported. All reported results are Groq / `gpt-oss-120b` only.
2. **Two complete one-call runs, not three.** The planned three runs per
   profile were reduced to two complete runs because of rate limiting
   (run 2 failed with infrastructure errors). The stability estimate and the
   ±SD figures therefore rest on n = 2 runs.
3. **Run 1 is excluded.** It is complete but was produced by the earlier
   two-call harness, so it is not comparable with the reported one-call runs.
   This is stated explicitly rather than silently dropped.
4. **Benchmark composition.** 15 of the 19 defective cases are ambiguity;
   the other three categories have n ≤ 2, so per-category results for them
   are not statistically meaningful.
5. **No inter-rater reliability.** Two blind annotators and
   `scripts/02_interrater_kappa.py` are still needed for a kappa value.
6. **No survey/SUS denominators yet** (`scripts/05_survey_and_sus.py` needs
   the raw Forms export and the 10 SUS rows).
7. **Recall is reported at one operating point.** The threshold sweep is
   included so the precision/recall trade-off is visible, but the paper
   should present 0.90 as the pre-registered threshold, not as an optimum
   chosen on the test set.
